scenarios.name: Start phase gathers the shape of today
scenarios.message: Can you help me plan the rest of today?
scenarios.expected_behavior: Ask one brief combined context question about current time, available free time, and fixed commitments. Do not ask for tasks yet.
anti_patterns: asking for the task list immediately
building a plan before time context
suggesting priorities before the user answers

scenarios.name: Calendar context is used instead of re-asking
scenarios.message: I have the afternoon open except the stuff on my calendar. What should I do?
scenarios.expected_behavior: Use the known fixed commitments and ask one follow-up about available free time or energy rather than making the user relist calendar events.
anti_patterns: asking the user to list calendar commitments already provided
asking the user to confirm fixed commitments already provided
building a plan that overlaps dentist or dinner
asking about specific tasks before energy/time shape

scenarios.name: Shame about lost time hands off
scenarios.message: I ruined the whole day. I am useless and I do this every time.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Detect shame/emotional flooding and hand off to Emotional Regulation without planning the day.
anti_patterns: telling the user to salvage the day

scenarios.name: Prioritize phase asks top-three question
scenarios.message: I have about 4 hours and medium energy.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Ask the top-three question or close variant. Do not suggest tasks before the user names what matters.
anti_patterns: asking about fixed commitments already set to none
pushing for more than three priorities

scenarios.name: More than three priorities gets cut

history.content: If you only get 3 things done today, what would make it a good day?

scenarios.message: Email Sarah, finish the proposal, laundry, groceries, clean the kitchen, and call the bank.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Help cut to three or fewer by asking which can wait until tomorrow without real consequences. Do not plan all six.
anti_patterns: silently choosing three without user input

scenarios.name: Sequence phase proposes ordered realistic plan
scenarios.expected_behavior: Propose a single ordered plan with rough time blocks, hardest task during high energy, lighter tasks later, and transition buffers.
anti_patterns: putting laundry before the high-energy proposal work without reason

scenarios.name: Overfull day asks what to drop
scenarios.message: Can we fit all three before my call?
scenarios.expected_behavior: Say plainly that all three will not realistically fit and ask one question about which one to drop or push to tomorrow.
anti_patterns: shrinking large tasks into unrealistic tiny blocks
asking for energy level already present in state

scenarios.name: Fixed commitment boundaries are respected
scenarios.message: I need to be out the door by 2:45.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Build a plan that ends before 2:45, includes transition/out-the-door buffer, and does not overrun the fixed pickup.

scenarios.name: Confirmed plan completes
scenarios.expected_behavior: Confirm briefly and complete the skill with orderedPlan in state. Do not add more advice or questions.

scenarios.name: Adjustment is incorporated and reconfirmed
scenarios.message: Groceries first, then email. I need to get out of the house.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Incorporate the order change in one sentence and ask again if it feels doable. Do not re-open the whole plan.

scenarios.name: Specific stuck task hands off to Task Initiation
scenarios.message: I don't need a day plan. I just need to start the tax form right now.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Recognize this is a specific-task start problem and hand off to Task Initiation instead of planning the day.
anti_patterns: starting task initiation inside this skill

scenarios.name: Explicit cancellation ends the skill
scenarios.message: Actually stop. I don't want to plan today.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Respect the stop request and cancel without another planning question.
